issues.title: Hardware acceleration breaks YouTube/video playback on Ryzen 9950X iGPU due to default 512MB UMA Frame Buffer Size
issues.author: Patrick Martel
issues.description:
Environment:

- OS: Debian Forky
- Browser: Brave Browser (Chromium-based)
- Hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X with Integrated Radeon Graphics
- Kernel Driver: amdgpu

Problem:

With hardware acceleration enabled, YouTube fails to render properly giving artifacts. Current workarounds are disabling hardware acceleration and/or changing the ANGLE graphics backend.

Root Cause & Solution:

The issue stems from the motherboard's default BIOS configuration for "UMA Frame Buffer Size" being set to "Auto", which defaults the baseline dedicated VRAM to 512MB.

Manually changing the BIOS setting "UMA Frame Buffer Size" from "Auto" to "1GB" (or higher) and reverting all browser workarounds back to default completely resolves the issue for me.

Can others confirm?

issues.title: iMac 17,1 - MCLK DPM quirk on R9 M380 Mac Edition (Bonaire, subsystem 0x106B) pins memory at 300 MHz boot clock — SMU reports phantom 1568 MHz, ~5x bandwidth loss
issues.author: cicciomazz
issues.description:
> **_Follow-up of #3425: the MCLK-DPM quirk added there works, but it pins this SKU's memory\
> to the 300 MHz boot clock, costing \~5x memory bandwidth. This is a kernel power-management\
> issue, not a RADV/Mesa one (cross-posted from the Mesa RADV issue)._**

## **TL;DR**

The MCLK DPM quirk for this board pins the R9 M380's memory to its 300 MHz boot clock:\
measured bandwidth is \~14 GB/s (\~73% of the 19.2 GB/s theoretical peak at 300 MHz on a\
128-bit GDDR5 bus), while SCLK runs at full 1021 MHz and the driver reports a phantom\
1568 MHz. Result: \~5x memory bandwidth loss vs Windows on the same silicon, and \~5x\
per-pixel render cost in games. Instrumented SMU tests show that every route which makes\
the 1568 MHz DPM level selectable kills the SMU7 firmware (immediately or within minutes)\
— the failure is inside the firmware's memory-clock transition, not in the driver's\
enable, voltage, or ACPI paths. The legacy radeon driver dies at the same SMU message.\
Open questions at the end.

## **1. Hardware / software**

* Apple iMac 27" Late 2015 (iMac17,1), i5-6500, 12 GB RAM, HDD.
* dGPU: AMD Radeon R9 M380 Mac Edition (Bonaire XT / Saturn XT, GCN 1.1 / CIK /\
  GFX7), PCI 1002:6640, subsystem 106b:014b, revision 0x80, 2 GB GDDR5 on a\
  128-bit bus. VBIOS Apple 113-C6005T-009, build 323656, ver\

## Summary

When an RDNA 4 GPU (RX 9060 XT, `1002:7590`) is connected via a Thunderbolt eGPU dock, any GPU reset attempt (triggered by GFX ring timeout under 3D load) causes a hard system lock requiring power cycle. The PCIe hot-reset does not propagate correctly through the Thunderbolt bridge chain, leaving the PCIe link in a bad state where any subsequent MMIO access hangs the CPU.

## Brief summary

```
RIP: dal_ddc_open+0x8c/0x150 [amdgpu]
BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000028
Workqueue: events_highpri dm_irq_work_func [amdgpu]
note: kworker/1:0H[29] exited with irqs disabled
```

issues.author: maxivau

**Brief summary of the problem:**

Running a sustained DirectX 12 workload (via vkd3d-proton) on the RX 9070 XT triggers a ring gfx_0.0.0 timeout that the driver cannot recover from with a soft/per-ring reset. The reset always fails (Ring gfx_0.0.0 reset failed, MES(1) failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE, failed to unmap legacy queue), forcing a full MODE1 reset, which reports VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!. The desktop compositor (GNOME Shell/Xwayland) loses its GPU context and crashes with SIGABRT, killing the entire graphical session — even though the GPU itself does recover afterward ("device wedged, but recovered through reset").

This is fully reproducible: it has occurred in every sustained session over roughly a dozen occurrences, always exactly once per session, on three different kernels (Ubuntu HWE 7.0.0-30, and mainline stable builds up to 7.2.2). Onset is load-dependent rather than time-fixed — typically 20–90 minutes into a session. One dmesg line points at the likely root cause: The CPFW hasn't support pipe reset yet. — i.e. the current CP firmware doesn't support gfx12 pipe reset, so the driver has no soft-recovery path and must escalate straight to the VRAM-losing MODE1 reset.

issues.author: Mikhail Gavrilov
issues.description:
A band of pixel noise flashes across the screen at random on a 3840x2160@120 display driven by an RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, DCN32). Each occurrence lasts exactly one frame — 8.3 ms — which is why it reads as a flicker rather than as corruption.

The artefact predates the 7.3 merge window but was rare. Since `a637a140ab86 ("drm/amd/display: Allocate DCN32/1 dmub memory to GTT")` it is about **35x more frequent**, measured against that commit's immediate parent with the CRTC CRC engine. The workaround has degraded too: one brief 120 → 60 → 120 toggle used to clear it every time, and now several toggles are needed, or about an hour spent at 60 Hz.

Mailing list thread: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260829010525.29935-1-mikhail.v.gavrilov@gmail.com/

## What it looks like

![PXL_20260823_205637668_2_00_00_11](/uploads/4e8440ab913a845322e6ff0dab0351c2/PXL_20260823_205637668_2_00_00_11.png){width=900 height=507}

![PXL_20260823_205637668_2](/uploads/66078fe398673754cb01ae325ac5a2d1/PXL_20260823_205637668_2.mp4){width=900 height=507}

The artefact never appears in a screenshot or a screen recording, so the attachments are a phone photo and a phone video of the panel.

## How it was measured

## 1. `DCIO_GSL0_CNTL` is written through a per-CRTC offset

`dce110_timing_generator_setup_global_swap_lock()` programs the global swap lock's vsync source with:

```c

issues.author: Curtis Vogt
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

amdgpu's Display Core supports the DRM EDID override layer (`drm.edid_firmware` / `edid_override`), but only consults it when it is _not_ doing its own hardware read. When it detects a present sink it reads the EDID over the wire (via `dm_helpers_read_local_edid`), and if that read returns `EDID_NO_RESPONSE` (logged as `EDID err: 2`) it synthesises a fallback mode rather than falling back to the override configured by the user. ## Summary

issues.title: deadlock on hibernation in ttm_device_prepare_hibernation() -> throttle_direct_reclaim()
issues.author: Maciej S. Szmigiero
issues.description:
From time to time I get a deadlock when hibernating a machine with amdgpu in `amdgpu_device_prepare()` -> `amdgpu_device_evict_resources()` -> `ttm_device_prepare_hibernation()` -> `ttm_tt_swapout()` -> `shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp()` -> `shmem_get_folio_gfp()` -> `shmem_alloc_and_add_folio()` -> `try_to_free_pages(`) -> `throttle_direct_reclaim()`.

And `throttle_direct_reclaim()` just waits forever for `kswapd` to make progress, which never happens so the machine is essentially deadlocked. 

Looking at the hibernation code it seems that the `prepare` callbacks 
happens *after* tasks are already frozen so no wonder `kswapd` will never make progress.

----

This was reproduced on the latest upstream kernel 7.1.3 but the current drm code does _not_ seem to have any material differences there.

Note this does NOT seem to be duplicate of #5470 since this does _not_ look like memory corruption, just deadlock with page reclaim code.

Also, this does not seem specific to particular type of a amdgpu GPU.

On an HDMI CTA mode with the `Broadcast RGB` connector property at its default `Automatic`, amdgpu

A sink that honours the InfoFrame expands 16-235 to 0-255: everything below code 16 is crushed to

issues.title: Poweroff/reboot hang: deadlock between amdgpu_dm_ism_disable() and dm_ism_delayed_work_func (DCN 3.5, 100% reproducible)
issues.author: Xell Pher
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

Laptop gets stuck on shutdown/reboot with screens off and status LEDs still on, power is not cut. Only hard power off (pressing the power button) makes it shut off completely.

Shutdown reaches amdgpu_pci_shutdown → amdgpu_device_suspend → dm_suspend → amdgpu_dm_ism_disable(), which holds the ISM mutex while calling disable_delayed_work_sync(). The pending dm_ism_delayed_work_func (events_unbound) tries to take that same mutex and blocks:

`INFO: task kworker/u64:10:3985 is blocked on a mutex likely owned by task shutdown:1`

hung_task fires after 120 s and panics (kernel.hung_task_panic=1). Looks like a lock/work-flush ordering problem in amdgpu_dm_ism_disable(): it flushes the work while holding the mutex the work acquires.

100% reproducible on every shutdown/reboot.

Hardware: Lenovo 21WVCTO1WW, BIOS R38ET26W (1.06), DCN 3.5 iGPU, Secure Boot on (kernel lockdown).

Kernel: 7.0.0-31-generic #31-Ubuntu -\> Tried amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x10 — no effect.

Workaround: modprobe -r / unbind amdgpu via a systemd ExecStop before shutdown → clean poweroff every time.
